newsitem.title: RUSSIA: BASKETBALL-YELTSIN STEPS IN TO HELP UNPAID DYNAMO.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-YELTSIN STEPS IN TO HELP UNPAID DYNAMO.

text.p: Sports-loving President Boris Yeltsin stepped in on Wednesday to help the unhappy basketball players of Dynamo Moscow, who have not been paid since summer.

Yeltsin signed a decree ordering the government to return state assets, including sports facilities, to the Dynamo club, a sprawling organisation which, as in Soviet times, is run by and for the police and other security forces.

Earlier in the day, the club's professional basketball players dropped a threat to strike and agreed to play Thursday's EuroLeague match against Spain's Caja San Fernando after national federation officials promised action in the dispute.

"The team decided we'll turn out tomorrow and in the last match of our EuroLeague group and will, naturally, play to win each game. There's no point adding anything," Dynamo player Oleg Meleshchenko told Russia's NTV television.
The Russian Basketball Federation said the players had been told a schedule for paying them the money owed to them would be worked out in a week, Itar-Tass news agency reported.
Federation president Sergei Belov urged the long-suffering players to abandon their planned strike in the name of patriotism, NTV said.
It said the players, unpaid since July, had been told on Tuesday their wages were being almost halved and they would have to pay their own taxes out of what was left.
Some are considering transfers to more prosperous clubs.
The Dynamo players are by no means the only Russians to suffer. Millions of Russians are in the same position as a web of company debts, unpaid wages and tax arrears ensnares the creaking economy.
